HEEWON STYLE — a TENEBRIST OIL PAINTING of a relationship, a 2:1 movie still composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). CLOSE-UP TWO-SHOT: the frame cut at the chest, both faces LARGE and filling the middle band, the hands that carry the gesture in frame, against a near-BLACK background — deep umber-indigo darkness with at most a faint suggestion of the place. ONLY THESE TWO PEOPLE in the whole frame: no onlookers, no blurred heads or shoulders in the foreground, no crowd. Painted like the house benchmark (a Gaya queen in gold-ornamented hair cradling her king’s head against her neck on a night ridge): one continuous oil painting, loaded broken-colour strokes dragged across the silk, thick impasto on lit folds, gold ornaments and jewels, and the FACES PAINTED TOO — softly modelled in warm oil glazes with visible brushwork on cheek and jaw, Korean-drama beauty, keeping the attached portraits’ eye shape and features; not flat cel shading, not a photograph. A Korean historical drama painted by Caravaggio and Rembrandt. ONE practical light close to the figures, raking from the side or below; 80% of the canvas sinks into shadow. The LAYOUT, BLOCKING, BODY LANGUAGE and FACIAL EXPRESSIONS convey the relationship instantly, without words: who is higher, who touches whom, where each one looks, one gesture that is the whole bond. SHE SEWS HIS TORN COAT SO SLOWLY HE CANNOT LEAVE. Night, a small sewing room, one candle. Young Chunchu stands very still, chin lifted, looking down at her, breath held, ears flushed. Munhee stands pressed close against his chest, mending the torn collar of his magenta coat right under his throat, her eyes lowered on the stitch, a tiny knowing smile; her lips almost at his throat. ONE DEVICE: one silk thread pulled taut from her needle to his collar, catching the candlelight — the line that binds him. The candle below rakes across her fingers, the needle, his jaw and both faces. REFERENCE SHEET (faces and garments only — invent new poses): LEFT of the sheet = ch_chunchu_hwarang.png; MIDDLE of the sheet = ch_munhee.png; RIGHT of the sheet = bn_munhee.png. CANON — KIM CHUNCHU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_chunchu_hwarang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). As a hwarang he keeps the crescent-moon headband across the brow, its tails trailing; the jougwan sits on the crown of the head above it. Now: Young hwarang (stage portrait): beardless, eager. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | MUNHEE — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munhee.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_munhee.png when the head is visible. Demeanor: Yushin's younger sister, Chunchu's wife; quick and warm, the one who bought the dream. #E07FA8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: fantasy tiara instead of her binyeo. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap): a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 75–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black; ONE hard directional practical key, close to the subjects and raking across the surfaces the camera sees from below or the side, never from behind them, carves both faces out of the dark. Every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side one opaque loaded stroke, the turn a crisp painted edge, the shadow a thin transparent umber glaze; gold thread, jewels and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beards, knuckles and armour plates painted the same way. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF: thick oil impasto and canvas grain over everything. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who is higher and who is lower, contact or distance, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. DEPTH: the subjects razor-sharp, the background melting into black haze with a few round painted bokeh discs from small lights. COLOR SYMBOLISM: each person’s hex lives in the key light and specular on them; the rest desaturated umber, slate and black. Not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura or emissive skin — character hex is the colour of REAL LIGHT.
